scene.note: Passes and the timetable work with real dates, counted in real months and days, and printed in English anywhere.

steps.note: A day and a time arrive as text, or as the three numbers written on the clipboard.
They become one date and time, or one date, that Java can count with.
A day that does not exist, or a time written another way, is refused with a message that quotes it.
A pass starts on the day it was bought, and runs for whole months.
Its last day keeps the day of the month, or moves to the end of a shorter month.
The passenger is told the days left from the day they ask, and a crossing is measured in minutes, midnight or not.
A day comes to the timetable as a date.
Its heading is written out in English, whatever language the computer speaks.
The timetable says whether boats run that day: every day but Sunday.
